lesson.title: Build a number from blocks
lesson.subtitle: Hundreds, tens and ones
lesson.story: Each column groups blocks by value. A hundreds block represents 100, a tens rod represents 10 and a ones counter represents 1. An empty column represents zero in that place.
lesson.objective: Read base-ten models and reason about the hundreds place.

steps.title: Find the place
hints: Each block in the hundreds column represents 100.

steps.title: Read the model
steps.prompt: What number do all the blocks represent?
hints: Look at the hundreds place, then the other columns.
The hundreds place uses groups of 100.
There are 2 blocks in the hundreds column; each represents 100.

steps.title: Explain the place
steps.prompt: Why does a digit need a named place?

choices.label: The place tells us how much each digit represents.
Every digit stands for single ones, wherever it sits.
Zero means the other columns must also be empty.

hints: Look at the different column units.
A hundreds block and a ones counter have different values.
The place tells us whether to count hundreds, tens or ones.
Choose: The place tells us how much each digit represents.
